nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How far from the top of the limestone cliff were the surveys conducted?
nodes.answer: Surveys were conducted between 50 and 100 meters from the top of the cliff.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Coral reef protection|Reef mapping_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What methods were used to assess the current distribution of Gongolaria barbata?
nodes.answer: The current distribution was established through an extensive survey conducted by snorkelling along approximately 30 km of coastline, along with GIS analysis.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Coral reef protection|Reef mapping_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How were the locations of Gongolaria barbata recorded during the field work?
nodes.answer: All the G. barbata populations were geolocalised and recorded on 1:2 500 maps.
